svg.title: Three regions: control, influence, and neither
svg.desc: Concentric circles diagram showing what a teacher controls, what they can influence, and the third region of what they do not control, with a note that most frustration comes from effort spent in that third region.
svg.text: Third region: what you do not control
pay scales . class size . the electricity supply . the examination system
Second region: what you can influence
a colleague's practice . a head's decision
a departmental habit
First region: what you control
how you prepare . how you speak to a pupil
the first ten minutes . what you read
who you ask for help
Where frustration comes from
Most professional frustration is effort spent in the
THIRD region: arguing with a pay scale, or waiting
for a class size to change before teaching well.
And the opposite failure
Naming the third region accurately is not the same
as being excused by it. The characteristic failure of
an experienced teacher in a hard system is to use a
true judgement about region three to justify doing
nothing in region one.
The three regions exhaust the situation
Every part of a teacher's working life sits in exactly
one of them. There is no fourth place to stand.
The regions are not fixed. A teacher who builds standing over a term moves items from the third region into the second.
